questions.q: What problem does ROW_NUMBER() have that RANK() and DENSE_RANK() fix?
options: ROW_NUMBER() always produces unique numbers, misrepresenting genuine ties as if one row beat the other
ROW_NUMBER() cannot be combined with PARTITION BY
ROW_NUMBER() requires GROUP BY, unlike RANK and DENSE_RANK
ROW_NUMBER() is deprecated in modern SQL Server
questions.explain: Both RANK() and DENSE_RANK() give tied rows the same number instead of arbitrarily breaking the tie.

questions.q: If two rows tie for rank 1 using RANK(), what rank does the next row get?
options: 3 — RANK() skips ahead by the size of the tie
2 — no gap is left
1 — the same as the tied rows
It depends on ORDER BY direction
questions.explain: RANK() leaves a gap exactly the size of the tie before continuing to the next rank.

questions.q: If two rows tie for rank 1 using DENSE_RANK(), what rank does the next distinct value get?
options: 2 — no gap is left, since DENSE_RANK() counts distinct values
3 — same gap behavior as RANK()
1 — the same rank as the tie
It cannot be determined without PARTITION BY
questions.explain: DENSE_RANK() ignores how many rows shared a rank — it just counts distinct values in sequence.

questions.q: When would ROW_NUMBER() be the better choice over RANK() or DENSE_RANK()?
options: When ties are impossible or irrelevant to the question being asked
Whenever the data contains any ties at all
ROW_NUMBER() should never be used once RANK/DENSE_RANK are known
Only when combined with GROUP BY
questions.explain: If ties don't matter for the use case, ROW_NUMBER() is the simplest of the three options.

questions.q: What question should guide the choice between RANK() and DENSE_RANK()?
options: Whether a tie should genuinely 'cost' a rank (skip ahead) or not (no gap) for the real-world scenario
Which function runs faster in all cases
Whether the data has more than 100 rows
Whether PARTITION BY is present
questions.explain: A sales leaderboard skipping 3rd place after a 2nd-place tie (RANK) differs from wanting gap-free distinct tiers (DENSE_RANK).
